newsitem.title: USA: Glenn announces he will not seek reelection.
newsitem.headline: Glenn announces he will not seek reelection.

text.p: Four-term Democratic senator John Glenn said Thursday he will not seek reelection, citing his age.
The 75-year-old Glenn made the announcement in his home town, 35 years to the day after he became the first American to orbit the Earth. He was first elected to the Senate in 1974.

Glenn's decisions opens the way for a fight for his seat. Republicans think they have a good chance of winning it, perhaps with popular two-term gov. George Voinovich who has already laid out plans for the race though has not formally announced as a candidate.

Glenn, in an address at Muskingum College, said his health remained excellent and his passion to serve was undiminished. But he said he would be 83 by the time he finished a fifth term. For that reason and no other, he said, he would retire.
Glenn, the only Ohioan ever elelcted to the Senate for four times, ran unsuccessfully for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1984.
